newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM criticises finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM criticises finance minister.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chenromyrdin attacked Finance Minister Alexander Livshits on Wednesday over a newspaper interview, fuelling speculation Livshits would be sacked in a forthcoming cabinet reshuffle.

"If it is true what is written in the newspaper, than it is gross misconduct on behalf of the finance minister. We will not tolerate this," Chernomyrdin told the Federation Council upper house of parliament.

Livshits said in an interview published by the Argumenty i Fakty weekly that regional governors should not divert government funds intended to pay pensions for other purposes, and complained about intense lobbying of the finance ministry.
"Those who wage a war against us... want the minister to obey. They say -- 'Give the money to them. Give it to me. Don't give it to those,'" Livshits said.
The liberal daily Sevodnya said on Wednesday that Chernomyrdin had agreed with President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday to dismiss Livshits in the reshuffle.
Sevodnya said the two had also agreed to make Yeltsin's chief of staff Anatoly Chubais, the sole first deputy prime minister.
A presidential spokesman said on Tuesday Yeltsin had approved proposals by Chernomyrdin for changes in the government but gave no details.
The reshuffle is expected to be announced after Yeltsin delivers a keynote speech to parliament on Thursday. The cabinet is due to meet soon after the speech.
Livshits, 50, was Yeltsin's chief economic adviser until being appointed to the cabinet last August after Yeltsin's election victory.
